note: Colors sampled from the three physical charts. Values marked decorativeOnly FAIL text contrast on white and must never carry text or act as the sole indicator of state.

ink.use: All body text, outlines, character linework. 15.8:1 on white.

chartTitleGreen.use: Chart title — Finley and Arthur. 6.4:1 on white, passes AA.

chartTitleRed.use: Chart title — Maryn. 4.9:1 on white, passes AA for body text.

completionMark.use: The hand-drawn checkmark. Keep it black and hand-drawn in feel — this is the single most recognizable element of the physical system.

identityColorResolution.conflict: Two color systems exist in the physical materials. The mascot artwork implies one palette (Finley orange, Arthur green, Maryn red); the FAMILY CHORE CHART legend explicitly assigns another (Finley blue, Arthur green, Maryn orange). Finley genuinely conflicts, and the mascot palette would put Finley's orange right next to Maryn's red — nearly indistinguishable at dot size.
identityColorResolution.resolution: The rotation-chart legend wins. It is an explicit, already-in-use family convention for identifying a child at a glance, and it is the only one of the two that is actually color-encoded on the wall. Mascot colors are demoted to decorative illustration fill only.
identityColorResolution.correction: Two contrast figures in an earlier draft of this file were wrong. Measured: mascot orange #D9642E is 3.61:1 and mascot green #5C8A33 is 4.09:1 on white — both FAIL AA for text. Neither may carry text. The values below are measured, not estimated.

identity.use: CANONICAL. Dot fill, text, event colors, widget accent — all uses. Passes AA and AAA.
Dot fill ONLY — matches the printed legend exactly. Never text.

identityText.use: CANONICAL for text, labels, and any stateful UI carrying Arthur's identity. Reads as the same green, passes AA.

identity.use: Dot fill ONLY — matches the printed legend exactly. Falls just short of AA; never text.

identityText.use: CANONICAL for text, labels, and any stateful UI carrying Maryn's identity.

typography.note: The physical charts use a rounded marker-style display face for the title and a plain humanist sans for chore text. Reproduce with system fonts so Dynamic Type works — do not ship a custom display font unless it supports the full Dynamic Type range.

cardFrames.open-book: Finley. Two facing pages, one chore per page. Naturally caps a day at two chores — respect that limit or the metaphor breaks.
cardFrames.bamboo-fence: Arthur. Chores listed on a horizontal bamboo rail with the panda peeking over the top.
cardFrames.held-sign: Maryn. A plain rectangular sign held up by the penguin, chores stacked vertically.

layout.grid: Seven day cards: four in the top row, three in the bottom row. Preserve this on iPad and Mac — it is what the family already reads at a glance. Collapse to a vertical list on iPhone and Watch only.
